category.name: Technology
category.description: Reporting, analysis, reviews, and teaching about software, devices, AI, security, and the systems shaping technology.

items.name: Stratechery
items.best_for: technology strategy and platform business analysis
items.reason: Ben Thompson connects product decisions, distribution, market structure, and platform power in a consistent analytical framework.
items.limitation: Much of the complete analysis and archive access requires a paid subscription.

items.name: Simon Willison's Weblog
items.best_for: hands-on AI, Python, data, and open-source experiments
items.reason: Simon Willison publishes reproducible technical notes, code, demos, and source links quickly enough to make a fast-moving field inspectable.
items.limitation: The chronological notebook format can require more reader context than a structured beginner guide.

items.name: The Pragmatic Engineer
items.best_for: software engineering careers, teams, and industry practice
items.reason: Gergely Orosz turns engineering-management reporting, interviews, and operator evidence into practical explanations for working developers.
items.limitation: Many complete reports and deep dives are available only to paid subscribers.

items.name: Daring Fireball
items.best_for: Apple, interface, and technology-industry commentary
items.reason: John Gruber combines close product observation with a distinctive editorial position and a long, searchable record of corrections and follow-up.
items.limitation: The Apple-centered lens and link-blog format are narrower than a general technology publication.

items.name: Krebs on Security
items.best_for: cybercrime investigations and security incident reporting
items.reason: Brian Krebs produces original reporting on breaches, fraud networks, identity crime, and the people and infrastructure behind security incidents.
items.limitation: The investigative focus is deliberately narrower than enterprise-security training or broad product coverage.

items.name: Schneier on Security
items.best_for: security policy, cryptography, risk, and public-interest analysis
items.reason: Bruce Schneier pairs technical security knowledge with policy context, primary links, and a durable archive that helps readers follow long-running issues.
items.limitation: The site mixes short linked commentary with longer analysis, so depth varies by post.

items.name: 404 Media
items.best_for: original investigations into technology, surveillance, and internet culture
items.reason: The worker-owned newsroom regularly produces source-led investigations that larger technology outlets follow and cite.
items.limitation: Some complete articles and community features are limited to paid members.

items.name: Platformer
items.best_for: social platforms, policy, moderation, and technology power
items.reason: Platformer reports on the decisions and institutions governing large online platforms, with a clear distinction between reporting and analysis.
items.limitation: Full access to some reporting and community discussions requires a subscription.

items.name: Benedict Evans
items.best_for: technology trends, market shifts, and strategic synthesis
items.reason: Benedict Evans uses market data, historical comparison, and compact models to separate durable platform shifts from short-term technology noise.
items.limitation: The high-level strategic view offers fewer implementation details for readers seeking tutorials.

items.name: Tedium
items.best_for: overlooked technology history and internet culture
items.reason: Ernie Smith researches ordinary technologies and forgotten web history deeply enough to make apparently minor subjects useful and memorable.
items.limitation: The deliberately eclectic subject selection is less useful for readers tracking one narrow industry beat.

items.name: WIRED
items.best_for: technology reporting with science, business, and cultural context
items.reason: WIRED combines original reporting, investigations, product coverage, and long-form analysis across technology's social and commercial consequences.
items.limitation: The broad remit and subscription model make depth and access uneven across sections.

items.name: Ars Technica
items.best_for: technically literate reporting on computing, policy, science, and security
items.reason: Ars Technica explains mechanisms and consequences with more technical depth than most general technology publications while maintaining a strong reporting desk.
items.limitation: Its detail and assumed background can feel dense for casual readers.

items.name: The Verge
items.best_for: consumer technology, platforms, policy, and product culture
items.reason: The Verge pairs fast reporting with strong visual storytelling, product expertise, and analysis of how technology changes everyday behavior.
items.limitation: Its editorial voice and high publishing volume can produce uneven depth across individual stories.

items.name: MIT Technology Review
items.best_for: emerging technology, AI, climate, biotechnology, and policy
items.reason: MIT Technology Review connects research and industry developments to public consequences with specialist reporting and an unusually clear evidence boundary.
items.limitation: A subscription is required for much of the complete reporting.

items.name: IEEE Spectrum
items.best_for: engineering, robotics, electronics, energy, and applied research
items.reason: IEEE Spectrum covers working technologies through engineers, specialist reporters, technical diagrams, and close attention to how systems are built.
items.limitation: Its engineering focus is narrower than general consumer or startup coverage.

items.name: Tom's Hardware
items.best_for: PC hardware testing, components, benchmarks, and buying decisions
items.reason: Tom's Hardware combines a deep testing archive with current component news, benchmark methodology, and practical system-building coverage.
items.limitation: Commercial buying coverage can overwhelm readers who want broader technology analysis.

items.name: TechCrunch
items.best_for: startups, venture capital, product launches, and technology business news
items.reason: TechCrunch maintains one of the broadest active reporting networks for startup funding, company changes, product announcements, and venture markets.
items.limitation: The speed and volume of coverage leave less room for depth in many daily stories.

items.name: Android Authority
items.best_for: Android devices, mobile software, testing, and buying guidance
items.reason: Android Authority combines a focused mobile beat with product testing, explainers, opinion, and a large archive of practical device guidance.
items.limitation: The consumer-device focus leaves limited room for broader software and technology policy.

items.name: Engadget
items.best_for: consumer electronics news, reviews, and major industry events
items.reason: Engadget maintains broad daily consumer-technology coverage with experienced reviewers and useful event reporting.
items.limitation: High publishing volume and commercial coverage make individual article depth inconsistent.

items.name: 9to5Mac
items.best_for: Apple news, software releases, devices, and ecosystem reporting
items.reason: 9to5Mac follows Apple products and software continuously, often surfacing release details and ecosystem changes before general outlets catch up.
items.limitation: Its narrow Apple focus and fast news cycle produce less value outside that ecosystem.
